/-!
# Albertson conjecture

The Albertson conjecture compares the crossing number and chromatic number of a finite simple
graph. It states that among graphs with a given chromatic number, the complete graph has the
smallest crossing number.

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albertson_conjecture)
-/

namespace AlbertsonConjecture

open Set
open scoped unitInterval

/--
A drawing of a finite simple graph in the plane. Vertices are represented by distinct points and
each edge by a simple continuous arc between its endpoints. The interior of an edge arc is not
allowed to pass through a vertex.
-/
structure PlaneDrawing {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) where
  vertex : Fin n → ℝ × ℝ
  vertex_injective : Function.Injective vertex
  edge : (e : G.edgeSet) → Path (vertex e.1.out.1) (vertex e.1.out.2)
  edge_injective : ∀ e, Function.Injective (edge e)
  edge_avoids_vertices : ∀ (e) (t : unitInterval) (v),
    edge e t = vertex v → v ∈ e.1

/-- The points traced by the interior of an edge in a plane drawing. -/
def PlaneDrawing.edgeInterior {n : ℕ} {G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)} (D : PlaneDrawing G)
    (e : G.edgeSet) : Set (ℝ × ℝ) :=
  D.edge e '' Ioo (0 : unitInterval) 1

/-- The points lying in the interiors of two distinct edges of a plane drawing. -/
def PlaneDrawing.crossingPoints {n : ℕ} {G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)} (D : PlaneDrawing G) :
    Set (ℝ × ℝ) :=
  {p | ∃ e₁ e₂ : G.edgeSet, e₁ ≠ e₂ ∧ p ∈ D.edgeInterior e₁ ∧ p ∈ D.edgeInterior e₂}

/--
A good drawing is a plane drawing with finitely many crossing points and with no point in the
interiors of three distinct edges. Thus every crossing point belongs to exactly two edge arcs and
is counted once.
-/
structure GoodDrawing {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) extends PlaneDrawing G where
  crossingPoints_finite : toPlaneDrawing.crossingPoints.Finite
  no_triple_crossing : ∀ (p : ℝ × ℝ) (e₁ e₂ e₃ : G.edgeSet),
    p ∈ toPlaneDrawing.edgeInterior e₁ →
    p ∈ toPlaneDrawing.edgeInterior e₂ →
    p ∈ toPlaneDrawing.edgeInterior e₃ →
    e₁ = e₂ ∨ e₁ = e₃ ∨ e₂ = e₃

/--
The crossing number of a finite simple graph is the minimum, over all good drawings in the plane,
of the number of crossing points.
-/
noncomputable def crossingNumber {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨅ D : GoodDrawing G, (D.toPlaneDrawing.crossingPoints.ncard : ℕ∞)

/--
**Albertson conjecture.** For every finite simple graph $G$, its crossing number is at least the
crossing number of the complete graph whose number of vertices is the chromatic number of $G$.
Equivalently, among all graphs with a given chromatic number, the complete graph has the smallest
crossing number.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem albertson_conjecture :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
      crossingNumber (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin G.chromaticNumber.toNat)) ≤ crossingNumber G := by
  sorry

end AlbertsonConjecture
modeling_decisions: Finite simple graphs are represented as `SimpleGraph (Fin n)`, which ranges over all finite simple graphs up to relabeling and ensures Mathlib's `chromaticNumber` is finite.

The list-entry formulation `cr(G) ≥ cr(K_{χ(G)})` is used directly. Since Mathlib's chromatic number has type `ℕ∞`, `G.chromaticNumber.toNat` supplies the ordinary natural chromatic number; this is valid for graphs on `Fin n`, which are finitely colorable.

A plane drawing sends distinct vertices to points of `ℝ × ℝ` and represents every unordered edge by an injective continuous unit-interval path between its endpoints. Edge interiors may not pass through vertices.

The crossing number is the infimum in `ℕ∞` of the finite numbers of crossing points over good drawings. Good drawings prohibit self-intersecting edges, infinitely many intersections, and triple crossings, so each crossing point is counted once. Using `ℕ∞` also avoids assigning a spurious value of zero if the drawing type were empty.
The strengthened formulation using Guy's conjectural formula and the weaker asymptotic formulation were intentionally omitted, as required by the source statement and decomposition.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Albertson conjecture

The Albertson conjecture (2007) relates the crossing number and the chromatic number of a
graph: among all graphs with chromatic number $r$, the complete graph $K_r$ has the smallest
crossing number. Equivalently, if $\chi(G) = r$ then $\operatorname{cr}(G) \ge
\operatorname{cr}(K_r)$.

The crossing number $\operatorname{cr}(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the minimum number of edge
crossings over all drawings of $G$ in the plane. Since Mathlib has no notion of a drawing of a
graph, this file defines drawings and the crossing number from scratch.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Albertson conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albertson_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Albertson, Cranston, Fox, *Colorings, crossings, and cliques*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1006.3783)
- [Barát, Tóth, *Towards the Albertson conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/0909.0413)
-/

namespace AlbertsonConjecture

open SimpleGraph
open scoped EuclideanGeometry

variable {V : Type*}

/-- A *drawing* of a simple graph `G` in the plane `ℝ²`: the vertices are placed at distinct
points, and each edge is represented by a simple arc (a continuous injective curve parametrised
by the unit interval) joining the points of its two endpoints and passing through no vertex
point in its interior. -/
structure Drawing (G : SimpleGraph V) where
  /-- The point of the plane at which the vertex `v` is placed. -/
  toFun : V → ℝ²
  /-- Distinct vertices are placed at distinct points. -/
  injective : Function.Injective toFun
  /-- The curve representing the edge `e`, parametrised by the unit interval `[0, 1]`. -/
  arc : G.edgeSet → unitInterval → ℝ²
  /-- Each edge is drawn as a continuous curve. -/
  continuous_arc (e : G.edgeSet) : Continuous (arc e)
  /-- Each edge is drawn as a simple arc, i.e. the curve does not cross itself. -/
  arc_injective (e : G.edgeSet) : Function.Injective (arc e)
  /-- The two ends of the arc of an edge are the points of the two endpoints of that edge. -/
  arc_endpoints (e : G.edgeSet) : s(arc e 0, arc e 1) = Sym2.map toFun e
  /-- The interior of the arc of an edge passes through no vertex point. -/
  arc_notMem_range (e : G.edgeSet) (t : unitInterval) (h₀ : t ≠ 0) (h₁ : t ≠ 1) :
    arc e t ∉ Set.range toFun

namespace Drawing

variable {G : SimpleGraph V} (D : Drawing G)

/-- The interior of the arc drawing the edge `e`: the arc without its two ends. -/
def arcInterior (e : G.edgeSet) : Set ℝ² :=
  D.arc e '' {t | t ≠ 0 ∧ t ≠ 1}

/-- The number of crossings of the drawing `D`, as an element of `ℕ∞`: the number of pairs
consisting of two distinct edges of `G` together with a point of the plane lying in the interiors
of both of their arcs. In a drawing in which no two edges touch without crossing, and no three
edges pass through a common point, this is exactly the number of edge crossings. -/
noncomputable def crossings : ℕ∞ :=
  {p : Sym2 G.edgeSet × ℝ² | ¬ p.1.IsDiag ∧ ∀ e ∈ p.1, p.2 ∈ D.arcInterior e}.encard

end Drawing

/-- The *crossing number* $\operatorname{cr}(G)$ of a graph `G`: the minimum number of edge
crossings over all drawings of `G` in the plane, as an element of `ℕ∞`. For a finite graph the
value is finite, since a straight-line drawing with the vertices in general position has finitely
many crossings. -/
noncomputable def crossingNumber (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨅ D : Drawing G, D.crossings

/-- A drawing of the edgeless graph has no crossings. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem Drawing.crossings_bot (D : Drawing (⊥ : SimpleGraph V)) : D.crossings = 0 := by
  rw [Drawing.crossings, Set.encard_eq_zero, Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem]
  rintro ⟨p, x⟩ -
  induction p using Sym2.ind with
  | h e f => simpa using e.2

/-- The edgeless graph on a countable vertex set has crossing number `0`. In particular the
drawings of a graph can exist, so `crossingNumber` is not vacuously `⊤`. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem crossingNumber_bot [Countable V] : crossingNumber (⊥ : SimpleGraph V) = 0 := by
  obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := Countable.exists_injective_nat V
  have hbot : ∀ e : (⊥ : SimpleGraph V).edgeSet, False := fun e => by simpa using e.2
  let D : Drawing (⊥ : SimpleGraph V) :=
    { toFun := fun v => EuclideanSpace.single 0 (f v : ℝ)
      injective := fun u v huv => by
        have h := congrArg (fun x : ℝ² => x 0) huv
        simp only [EuclideanSpace.single_apply, if_true, Nat.cast_inj] at h
        exact hf h
      arc := fun e => (hbot e).elim
      continuous_arc := fun e => (hbot e).elim
      arc_injective := fun e => (hbot e).elim
      arc_endpoints := fun e => (hbot e).elim
      arc_notMem_range := fun e => (hbot e).elim }
  exact le_antisymm (iInf_le_of_le D (Drawing.crossings_bot D).le) (zero_le _)

/-- **Albertson conjecture.** For every finite simple graph $G$ with chromatic number
$\chi(G) = r$, the crossing number of $G$ is at least the crossing number of the complete graph
$K_r$ on $r$ vertices:
$$\operatorname{cr}(G) \ge \operatorname{cr}(K_{\chi(G)}).$$
In other words, among all graphs with the same chromatic number as $G$, the complete graph has
the smallest crossing number. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem albertson_conjecture [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (r : ℕ)
    (hr : G.chromaticNumber = r) :
    crossingNumber (completeGraph (Fin r)) ≤ crossingNumber G := by
  sorry

end AlbertsonConjecture

modeling_decisions: Form of the conjecture: used the hypothesis `G.chromaticNumber = r` (Barát–Tóth: 'if χ(G) = r then cr(G) ≥ cr(K_r)'), which is the literal reading of 'a complete graph with the same chromatic number'. The Albertson–Cranston–Fox form with `r ≤ χ(G)` is equivalent given monotonicity of cr(K_r) in r but was not added as a separate variant.
Graphs are finite simple graphs (`[Fintype V]`, `SimpleGraph V`), as in all sources; K_r is `SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin r)`.

Crossing number lives in ℕ∞ (infimum over drawings of an ℕ∞-valued count). For finite graphs the value is finite (straight-line drawings in general position exist), so ⊤ is never reached in the conjecture; the inequality is compared in ℕ∞. `chromaticNumber` is also ℕ∞-valued in current Mathlib, hence the cast `(r : ℕ∞)`.

Crossings are counted as incidences (unordered pair of distinct edges, common interior point), via `Set.encard`. This equals the usual crossing count on 'good' drawings; on degenerate drawings it counts touchings, k-fold points with multiplicity C(k,2), and overlapping arcs as ⊤. None of these lower the infimum, and since only common interior points are counted (shared endpoints excluded, and arc interiors avoid vertex points), the infimum is exactly the standard crossing number. Counting pairs of edges instead would have yielded the pair crossing number, a different (conjecturally equal) invariant — deliberately avoided.
Drawings require edges to be simple arcs (injective continuous maps from unitInterval) and vertex placement injective, matching standard definitions; these restrictions do not change the minimum.
The plane is `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)` via the repo's scoped `ℝ²` notation (drawings in the plane and on the sphere give the same crossing number).

Two provable `@[category API]` lemmas (`Drawing.crossings_bot`, `crossingNumber_bot`) are included as sanity checks that the `Drawing` structure is inhabitable and that the edgeless graph has crossing number 0; they are not slots.

Definitions are kept in the problem file (inside `namespace AlbertsonConjecture`) because the task restricts output to the single candidate file; a reviewer may prefer moving `Drawing`/`crossingNumber` to FormalConjecturesForMathlib.

- [Wikipedia, Albertson conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albertson_conjecture)

  cliques*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1006.3783)

open scoped EuclideanGeometry unitInterval

namespace AlbertsonConjecture

variable {V : Type*}

/-- A drawing of a simple graph `G` in the plane. The vertices are placed at distinct points,
and each edge is represented by a simple arc (a continuous injective map from the unit interval)
whose endpoints are the images of the two endpoints of the edge and whose interior does not pass
through the image of any vertex. -/
structure Drawing (G : SimpleGraph V) where
  /-- The point of the plane at which a vertex is placed. -/
  vertex : V → ℝ²
  vertex_injective : Function.Injective vertex
  /-- The arc representing an edge. -/
  arc : G.edgeSet → I → ℝ²
  arc_continuous (e : G.edgeSet) : Continuous (arc e)
  arc_injective (e : G.edgeSet) : Function.Injective (arc e)
  /-- The endpoints of the arc of an edge are the images of the endpoints of the edge. -/
  arc_endpoints (e : G.edgeSet) : Sym2.map vertex e = s(arc e 0, arc e 1)
  /-- The interior of an arc does not pass through the image of any vertex. -/
  arc_interior_not_mem_range (e : G.edgeSet) (t : I) (ht : t ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1) :
    arc e t ∉ Set.range vertex

variable {G : SimpleGraph V}

/-- The crossings of a drawing: an unordered pair of distinct edges together with a point of the
plane lying in the interior of both of their arcs. -/
def Drawing.crossings (D : Drawing G) : Set (Sym2 G.edgeSet × ℝ²) :=
  {c | ∃ e f : G.edgeSet, e ≠ f ∧ c.1 = s(e, f) ∧
    c.2 ∈ D.arc e '' Set.Ioo 0 1 ∧ c.2 ∈ D.arc f '' Set.Ioo 0 1}

/-- The crossing number of a graph: the minimum number of crossings over all of its drawings in
the plane. This is `⊤` if the graph has no drawing, which cannot happen for finite graphs. -/
noncomputable def crossingNumber (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨅ D : Drawing G, D.crossings.encard

/-- A drawing of a graph with no edges has no crossings. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem Drawing.crossings_bot (D : Drawing (⊥ : SimpleGraph V)) : D.crossings = ∅ := by
  ext ⟨p, x⟩
  simp only [Drawing.crossings, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false]
  rintro ⟨⟨e, he⟩, -⟩
  simp at he

/-- A graph with no edges on a countable vertex set has crossing number zero. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem crossingNumber_bot [Countable V] : crossingNumber (⊥ : SimpleGraph V) = 0 := by
  obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := exists_injective_nat V
  have hbot : ∀ e : (⊥ : SimpleGraph V).edgeSet, False := fun e => by simpa using e.2
  let D : Drawing (⊥ : SimpleGraph V) :=
    { vertex := fun v => EuclideanSpace.single 0 (f v : ℝ)
      vertex_injective := fun v w hvw => by
        have := congrArg (fun p : ℝ² => p 0) hvw
        simpa [EuclideanSpace.single_apply, hf.eq_iff] using this
      arc := fun e => (hbot e).elim
      arc_continuous := fun e => (hbot e).elim
      arc_injective := fun e => (hbot e).elim
      arc_endpoints := fun e => (hbot e).elim
      arc_interior_not_mem_range := fun e => (hbot e).elim }
  rw [crossingNumber, ENat.iInf_eq_zero]
  exact ⟨D, by rw [D.crossings_bot, Set.encard_empty]⟩

/-- The crossing number is monotone: a drawing of `G` restricts to a drawing of any subgraph
`H ≤ G` with no more crossings. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem crossingNumber_mono {H : SimpleGraph V} (hHG : H ≤ G) :
    crossingNumber H ≤ crossingNumber G := by
  let ι : H.edgeSet → G.edgeSet := fun e => ⟨e, SimpleGraph.edgeSet_mono hHG e.2⟩
  have hι : Function.Injective ι := fun e f h => Subtype.ext (congrArg Subtype.val h :)
  refine le_iInf fun D => ?_
  let D' : Drawing H :=
    { vertex := D.vertex
      vertex_injective := D.vertex_injective
      arc := fun e => D.arc (ι e)
      arc_continuous := fun e => D.arc_continuous (ι e)
      arc_injective := fun e => D.arc_injective (ι e)
      arc_endpoints := fun e => D.arc_endpoints (ι e)
      arc_interior_not_mem_range := fun e => D.arc_interior_not_mem_range (ι e) }
  refine (iInf_le _ D').trans ?_
  have hinj : Function.Injective (Prod.map (Sym2.map ι) (id : ℝ² → ℝ²)) :=
    (Sym2.map.injective hι).prodMap Function.injective_id
  rw [← hinj.encard_image]
  refine Set.encard_le_encard ?_
  rintro ⟨p, x⟩ ⟨⟨q, y⟩, ⟨e, f, hef, rfl, hx1, hx2⟩, h⟩
  simp only [Prod.map, id, Prod.mk.injEq] at h
  obtain ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ := h
  exact ⟨ι e, ι f, fun h => hef (hι h), by simp, hx1, hx2⟩

Equivalently, among all graphs with chromatic number $n$, the complete graph $K_n$ has the

    crossingNumber (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin n)) ≤ crossingNumber G := by

Jordan arc joining the images of its endpoints and passing through no other vertex. A crossing

counted once for each pair of edges meeting there. The crossing number is the infimum of the
number of crossings over all drawings. Counting every such meeting of two arcs (including, say,
touchings) does not change this minimum, since a meeting that is not a transversal crossing can be
removed by redrawing, so this agrees with the usual crossing number.

- M. O. Albertson, D. W. Cranston, J. Fox, *Crossings, colorings, and cliques*,

- J. Barát, G. Tóth, *Towards the Albertson conjecture*,
  [arXiv:0909.0413](https://arxiv.org/abs/0909.0413)
-/

open SimpleGraph
open scoped EuclideanGeometry

namespace AlbertsonConjecture

variable {V : Type*}

/-- A *drawing* of a simple graph `G` in the plane `ℝ²`. Distinct vertices are represented by
distinct points, and each edge `s(u, v)` is represented by a Jordan arc (the range of an injective
path) from the point of `u` to the point of `v` that passes through no vertex point other than its
two endpoints. -/
structure Drawing (G : SimpleGraph V) where
  /-- The point of the plane representing a vertex. -/
  vertex : V → ℝ²
  vertex_injective : Function.Injective vertex
  /-- The arc of the plane representing an edge. -/
  arc : G.edgeSet → Set ℝ²
  /-- The edge `s(u, v)` is drawn as a Jordan arc from `vertex u` to `vertex v`. -/
  exists_path (u v : V) (h : G.Adj u v) : ∃ γ : Path (vertex u) (vertex v),
    Function.Injective γ ∧ Set.range γ = arc ⟨s(u, v), h⟩
  /-- The only vertex points on the arc of an edge are its two endpoints. -/
  mem_of_vertex_mem_arc (e : G.edgeSet) (w : V) : vertex w ∈ arc e → w ∈ (e : Sym2 V)

/-- The *crossings* of a drawing: an unordered pair of distinct edges together with a point of the
plane lying in the interior of both of their arcs. A point at which `k` arcs meet accounts for
`k.choose 2` crossings, as usual. -/
def Drawing.crossings {G : SimpleGraph V} (D : Drawing G) : Set (Sym2 G.edgeSet × ℝ²) :=
  {x | ¬ x.1.IsDiag ∧ ∀ e ∈ x.1, x.2 ∈ D.arc e \ Set.range D.vertex}

/-- The *crossing number* $\mathrm{cr}(G)$ of a graph `G`: the minimum number of crossings in a
drawing of `G` in the plane. It is an extended natural number; a drawing with infinitely many
crossings contributes `⊤`. -/
noncomputable def crossingNumber (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨅ D : Drawing G, D.crossings.encard

/-- The crossing number is at most the number of crossings of any drawing. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem crossingNumber_le_encard_crossings {G : SimpleGraph V} (D : Drawing G) :
    crossingNumber G ≤ D.crossings.encard :=
  iInf_le _ D

/-- A drawing of a graph without edges has no crossings. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem Drawing.crossings_bot (D : Drawing (⊥ : SimpleGraph V)) : D.crossings = ∅ := by
  ext ⟨s, p⟩
  induction s using Sym2.ind with
  | h e _ => simpa using e.2

/-- A graph without edges on a countable vertex set has crossing number `0`. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem crossingNumber_bot [Countable V] : crossingNumber (⊥ : SimpleGraph V) = 0 := by
  obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := Countable.exists_injective_nat V
  let D : Drawing (⊥ : SimpleGraph V) :=
    { vertex := fun v => WithLp.toLp 2 fun _ => (f v : ℝ)
      vertex_injective := fun u v h => hf <| Nat.cast_injective <|
        congrFun (WithLp.toLp_injective 2 h) 0
      arc := fun e => (by simpa using e.2 : False).elim
      exists_path := fun _ _ h => h.elim
      mem_of_vertex_mem_arc := fun e => (by simpa using e.2 : False).elim }
  exact le_antisymm ((crossingNumber_le_encard_crossings D).trans_eq (by simp [D.crossings_bot]))
    (zero_le _)

crossing number is at least that of the complete graph on $r$ vertices:
$\chi(G) = r \implies \mathrm{cr}(G) \ge \mathrm{cr}(K_r)$. That is, the crossing number of a
graph is lower-bounded by the crossing number of the complete graph with the same chromatic
number. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem albertson_conjecture [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (r : ℕ)
    (hr : G.chromaticNumber = r) :
    crossingNumber (completeGraph (Fin r)) ≤ crossingNumber G := by
  sorry

end AlbertsonConjecture
